Changed file: internal/contextindex/eval_query.go

Intent:
harness: overlap the three read-only Git brackets a user-prompt event opens

A user-prompt event opens three independent GPK-V0-007 nonmutation brackets and
ran them strictly in series: the gokernel repository probe, the context index
build, and history learning. Sixteen Git processes, six of them
"status --porcelain -uall", every one of them serial.

None of the three consumes what another produces, and all three only read, so
each bracket still spans every read any of them issues -- a wider window that
must be found unchanged is a stronger nonmutation claim, not a weaker one.

- the probe now runs beside the index-backed context block instead of before it
  (its ProfileID is unused on every index-backed event; the block reads the
  repository through its own bracket). Error precedence is unchanged: the
  probes failure is still reported before the context blocks.
- history learning pairs its opening status read with its opening identity read,
  and its closing tree read with its closing status read -- the same idiom
  observeRepository already uses for the build.
- the opening history observation is issued by EvalQuery, ahead of the ranking
  pass, which reads only pinned index bytes and no repository at all.

Byte-identical stdout on both replayed corpora, and
conformance/cli-parity-v0 replays parity=100 with zero failures.

(cherry picked from commit 8f8c5900de60c556c18f4cbbdf6f34512aa69f41)

Changed file: internal/contextindex/index.go

Intent:
contextindex: count the symbols a rejected Python file loses, and stop rejecting f(.1)

Two defects, one failure mode: a Python source the closed grammar rejected lost
every symbol and import it carried, and nothing recorded that it had happened.

Observability. pythonSourceFacts discarded the grammar's refusal, so collect()
appended an empty symbol slice for a file that stayed counted in Sources. A file
the index could not read and a file that defines nothing produced byte-identical
evidence. Index.Unparsed now names every admitted source whose facts were
dropped, with a stable Reason a caller branches on (PYTHON_SOURCE_UNPARSED,
SOURCE_NOT_TEXT), the extractor's own refusal in Detail, and the BlobHash that
binds the loss to exact bytes. The same silent shape one branch above -- a source
whose bytes are not decodable text -- is recorded too. witness.coverage consults
the set, so a dropped .py reports NONE/PYTHON_SOURCE_UNPARSED on the receipt
instead of the language's nominal SHALLOW, which overstated what was analysed.
No verdict changes: both tiers were already non-DEEP and therefore NOT_RUN.

Grammar. The number lexer started a NUMBER only on a digit, so `.1` lexed as the
delimiter `.` followed by `1`, which no operand position admits. CPython 3.12's
tokenizer emits `.1` as one NUMBER; the lexer now makes the same test -- a dot
opens a number exactly when a digit follows it.

GPK-V0-033 adjudication for f(.1): go-defect. The oracle path for these symbols
is ast.parse (src/context_corvint_index.py:1092-1095), and CPython 3.12.14 accepts
f(.1), f(1, .2), f((.1)), f(.1e3), f(.1j) and print(.5) -- every one of which the
candidate rejected as MALFORMED_INPUT. The candidate contradicts the observable
the oracle defines, so Go is repaired and src/ is untouched.

Measured over 3,578 git-tracked .py files in the workspace: 11 rejections before,
10 after. corvint-soak/tests/test_soak.py is the file recovered, exactly as
reported. All 10 that remain are accepted by CPython 3.12 and so are further
false positives of the same class, now countable rather than silent; they are
reported for adjudication rather than repaired here, being separate grammar rules.

conformance/cli-parity-v0 passes: TestGPKV0002ManifestReplay PASS (373.01s),
parity=100, against a binary built from this tree rather than the stale
~/.local/bin/corvint.

Changed file: internal/contextindex/index.go

Intent:
contextindex: admit and extract Swift, Rust, C#, Kotlin and Ruby

The live index admitted 15 suffixes and extracted symbols from two of
them. Swift, Rust, C#, Kotlin and Ruby files were not merely unanalysed:
they were absent from Sources entirely, so nothing could search them.

Admission adds .rs .cs .swift .kt .kts .rb with symbol extraction, and
.sql .m as searchable text only -- SQL has no extractor here, and .m is
shared by Objective-C, MATLAB and Mathematica, so any symbol rule for it
would be right for at most one of the three.

Extraction is lexical, following goSymbols rather than parsing. A shared
carried-state scanner reduces each line to its code first, so comments,
string literals, raw strings and Rust lifetimes cannot be read as
declarations; the four brace languages then differ only by keyword table.
Ruby gets its own scanner for heredocs and =begin blocks.

Every give-up path is countable. The index gained ExtractionNotes, and
the receipt reports them beside its exclusions -- but only when non-empty,
so a clean receipt keeps its exact bytes. This is deliberate: the defect
worth avoiding is a walk that stops early and leaves the file counted as
indexed with nothing to declare, which is what pythonsymbols.go's
`return nil, nil` does today.

Coverage reports GENERIC, not SHALLOW. SHALLOW is Python's tier and
Python has a validated grammar yielding definitions and imports; these
languages get definitions only, from a line scanner. Given two existing
tiers, the honest direction to round is down, with a per-language reason
code carrying the detail.

Measured over 1,523 real files (beamfall-workspace): 25,626 symbols, 1
extraction note, and 0 false positives in a 45-per-language hand-check
after fixing four defects the corpus exposed -- C# delegates and events
named after their type, truncated qualified namespaces, and Kotlin
extension functions named after their receiver.

cli-parity-v0 passes unchanged (416.9s). The pinned corpus contains no
file in any newly admitted language, so admission cannot reach it, and
the receipt key is absent without notes.

Changed file: internal/contextindex/parse.go

Intent:
contextindex: lex JavaScript and TypeScript before extracting import edges

The shared genericImport scanner mirrors the frozen oracle's fallback
(src/context_corvint_index.py:1213-1217) and matches `from`/`import` plus a
quoted run anywhere in the bytes. Over 1,074 tracked web sources it invented 27
edges from comment text, string literals, and template-literal bodies -- one of
them a whole paragraph of program text recorded as a module name.

webImports gives the six web suffixes a lexer and reads a specifier from exactly
the three positions the regex targeted, so no new edge kind rides along.
Measured: 5,281 -> 5,257 edges over 980 files, 27 removed across three corpora,
zero added, every removal opened and confirmed fabricated. A file that ends
inside an unterminated block comment or template literal reports through the
existing Unparsed channel as WEB_SOURCE_UNPARSED rather than silently returning
a short set. Registered as DR-0011, python-defect, latent.

The file below was changed with the intent described. Which other file(s) in this repository must change alongside it?

Changed file: internal/gokernel/harness.go

Intent:
Ratify the 2026-08-29 brief in full (decision 0007)

The owner ratified all fourteen items. "Everything" is not self-executing:
three items recommend NOT changing a clause, one is a question of fact no
ratification can answer, and one was already resolved in code. Decision 0007
fixes what the ruling means item by item.

Clause changes landing with the record:

- GPK-V0-042 (new): a beta rung between opt-in candidate use and packaging Go
  as `corvint`. Per command, installed as `corvint`, third `BETA` matrix label,
  admission on the already-green GPK-V0-017 / W11 / W12 evidence. An open
  register entry blocks retirement contribution but not beta admission,
  provided the divergence is disclosed. GPK-V0-015 and every cutover gate are
  unweakened. Numbered 042, not the brief's predicted 041, which is taken.
- GPK-V0-027: impact widens from `.go` to "paths for which this specification
  names a reverse-import resolution rule", and names three (`.go`, `.py`, web).
  The five languages admitted for indexing on 2026-08-29 are explicitly NOT
  widened into: they have no oracle branch, so admitting them would create
  behaviour whose only authority is the candidate (GPK-V0-033).
- GPK-V0-028: `--limit` widens from exactly 1 to the inclusive range 1--10.
  The intent gate and the ASCII gate are deliberately untouched.
- GPK-V0-038: the harness `receiptId` is documented as a request identity, not
  an answer digest. The profile is NOT bumped; the flag day is deferred (D8=B).
- CF-V0-004: `EMPTY` and exit 0 are recorded unreachable in V0 rather than
  widening OCM-V0-001 in both runtimes to reach a state nothing needs (D12=B).
- analyzer-candidate-profiles: `go.mod`/`go.work` admit real patch versions over
  a stated 1.26.Z/1.27.Z range, Z in 0--99 (D7=A).
- rust-analyzer-candidate-v0: intent status proposed -> accepted (D6).
- python-retirement-execution: W15 checklist addendum for the `.claude`
  forbiddenParts divergence, whose measured impact is zero files (D10).

D3 is the one conditional ruling: DR-0005's re-measurement is authorized and
its adjudication pre-approved as A, unless the measurement contradicts A, in
which case it returns to the owner. A blanket yes there would have ratified a
conclusion about a measurement nobody has taken.

D11 needed nothing — the neutral `internal/pythonsyntax` route was already
taken and TestCoreDependencyClosureExcludesPythonCandidate passes. Its two
stale memory entries are deleted, and a third (DR-0005's) is corrected rather
than deleted, since its underlying work is still live under D3.

Verified before writing: pythonsyntax is called from lrfrepo/ocm.go:821, the
closure test passes, and `go build ./internal/gokernel/` is clean.
